# Client tests that are about real threads or real time. They start the loader's workers
# (`Loader::new`), the scene thread (`World::with_loader`) or a plain thread, and some of them wait
# on wall-clock time, so they do not gate merges (see docs/agents/ci.md). Every other test that
# streams runs stepped (`Loader::stepped`, `World::with_stepped_loader`: no threads, no sleeps, no
# machine clock) and gates.
#
# One test-name filter per line. libtest matches a filter anywhere in the full test name. The
# `linux` and `windows-tests` jobs `--skip` each line; the `real-thread-tests` job runs only these.
# Every client test therefore runs in exactly one of the two. A line that matches no test of the
# client binary, or a test of another crate, fails a check (.github/scripts/check-real-thread-list.sh).
#
# A new test goes here only if its point is a thread or the time: how long the frame thread waits,
# a worker that panics or races, a thread that is busy or parked. A test of what becomes resident,
# what is drawn, order, eviction or Edits is a stepped test.

# The two full-size runs (ignored by default): the frame thread's milliseconds over the whole Planet.
streaming_tests::the_full_size_planet_streams_in_and_walking_over_it_does_not_stall
streaming_tests::soft_misses_on_the_flight_take_off_and_standing_paths

# The scene thread's work of each frame, timed (what it prints is the point; the fill after it runs
# stepped in `after_walking_at_5_m_per_s_...`).
streaming_tests::walking_at_5_m_per_s_while_the_loader_runs_reports_the_scene_work_of_every_frame

# The frame thread's waits for the scene thread and for the store, in milliseconds.
streaming_tests::an_edit_the_frame_after_does_not_wait_for_slow_coarse_levels_and_reads_of_the_store_wait_a_step_at_most
streaming_tests::the_frame_thread_takes_a_few_milliseconds_of_the_largest_edit_at_the_spawn_with_every_wait

# A scene thread that is busy for real time, one that is parked and wakes itself, one that panics, and
# a result that is never lost to a thread that goes on publishing. The first stays here though the
# bound it checks has a stepped test (`an_edit_a_busy_scene_thread_has_not_packed_...`): only a real
# thread runs the frame thread's wait on the machine's clock (a condition variable's timeout).
streaming_tests::an_edit_the_scene_thread_is_too_busy_to_pack_shows_when_it_has_and_the_frame_does_not_wait
streaming_tests::a_parked_scene_thread_takes_the_coarsening_steps_back_when_the_hold_is_over
streaming_tests::a_panic_on_the_scene_thread_is_a_panic_on_the_frame_thread_not_a_wait
streaming_tests::a_job_that_is_done_is_always_there_to_be_taken_even_as_the_thread_goes_on_publishing

# A loader worker that panics.
loader::tests::a_worker_that_panics_panics_the_frame_thread_instead_of_loading_stopping_silently

# bins/client/src/priority.rs: spawns a thread to lower its priority (Linux only).
priority::tests::
